sections.h2: Where is Anderson County and how is it set up?
sections.html:
Anderson County sits in northwestern South Carolina along the Georgia line, in the Greenville-Anderson-Greer metropolitan area. It covers 755.76 square miles, and 41.91 of those are water.

The county seat and largest city is Anderson. The other cities are Belton, Clemson and Easley, and the last two are mostly in Pickens County. Towns include Honea Path, Iva, Pelzer, Pendleton, Starr, West Pelzer and Williamston. Powdersville, Homeland Park, Northlake and Sandy Springs are census-designated places.

Anderson County has a council-administrator government. Seven council members are elected from single-member districts to two-year terms, and the county's divisions include Finance and Planning. Sellers who need a permit history or zoning answer should start with those offices.

The council districts are named for areas of the county: North Anderson, South and East Anderson, the Belton, Starr and Iva area, the Pendleton area, West Anderson, the Powdersville area, and the Williamston and Honea Path area. That list is a quick way to see how the county thinks of its own geography, and it helps when you describe where a house sits to a county office.

sections.h2: What makes Lake Hartwell matter to a house sale?
sections.html:
Lake Hartwell is a 55,950-acre U.S. Army Corps of Engineers lake with nearly 1,000 miles of shoreline, per Wikipedia, for residential and recreational use. Lake Secession, the Saluda River and the Savannah River are also in the county.

A lakeside house has a different buyer pool than a mill-town house in Pelzer or a newer house near Powdersville. We have not sourced shoreline permit rules, dock rules or flood-zone data, so a lake seller should ask the county and the Corps what applies to a particular lot.

sections.h2: When are Anderson County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
South Carolina law lets counties collect property tax from September 30 to January 15, and a penalty starts after that. A 3% penalty applies from January 16 or 30 days after mailing, whichever is later, then 7% more from February 2 and 5% more from March 17, after which an execution is issued.

sections.h2: How does a reassessment notice work in Anderson County?
sections.html:
State law requires the county assessor to mail a notice when it raises a property's value by $1,000 or more or makes the first assessment on a parcel. The notice has to show market value, the assessment ratio, the acreage or lots, the tax map number and how to appeal.

The owner then has 90 days from the mailing to object in writing. In a countywide reassessment year, substantially all notices must go out by October 1. If they do not, the prior year's assessment is the basis for the current tax year.

  • Keep the notice, because the deadline runs from its mailing date.
  • Put your objection in writing and say which value or ratio you dispute.
  • In a year without a notice, you may appeal at any time in writing.
  • An appeal filed before the first penalty date applies to that tax year.

We did not open the Anderson County Assessor's pages, so we do not describe local forms or hearings. Ask that office which form to use and where to file it.

sections.h2: Why does a mailing address matter when a house is sold?
sections.html:
If title changes hands during a tax year and the county mailed the bill to the previous owner, the treasurer shall waive the penalty when the new owner got no timely notice. That is in S.C. Code 12-45-180(B).

The practical lesson is to update the address on file right away. A bill mailed to a deceased parent or a former owner can sit unopened until the penalty dates pass. Whoever holds the deed should confirm the address with the treasurer and assessor and ask for the balance in writing.

  • Give the treasurer your new mailing address after the deed is recorded.
  • Ask for the unpaid balance and the penalty dates in writing.
  • Keep your closing statement and any payment receipts together.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Anderson County?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest source of jobs, with 16,042 positions or 22.7% of the county total. Wikipedia reports more than 230 manufacturers in the county, including 22 international companies, and its early economy was built on textile mills processing cotton.

As of April 2024 some of the top employers were AnMed Health Medical Center, Anderson University, Bosch, the City of Anderson, Glen Raven, Ingles, Michelin, Walmart and Walgreens. The 2022 GDP was $9.1 billion, and unemployment ran near 3% from 2021 to 2024. Anderson University has about 4,000 students.

Anderson County was founded in 1826 after the Pendleton District was dissolved, and it is named for Revolutionary War general Robert Anderson. During the Civil War it became a center of ammunition production for the Confederate army.

Growth has been steady for a century, with the 1980 to 2020 gain at about 70,000 people. That steady growth means the county has both old mill-era housing and recently built subdivisions, which can mean very different repair needs from one street to the next.

sections.h2: How has the population changed, and what does the housing look like?
sections.html:
Anderson County had 203,718 people in 2020, up from 145,196 in 1990, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 219,930. There were 80,372 households and 89,123 housing units in 2020, with 9.8% vacant and 73.2% of occupied homes owner-occupied.

The median age was 41.1, and 18.9% of residents were 65 or older. Anderson County has five school districts, numbered 1 through 5, so the district for a house depends on its street. Ask the districts for a boundary lookup.

Roads include Interstate 85, U.S. 29, 76 and 178, and many state routes, and Anderson Regional Airport serves the county. Houses near I-85 and the Greenville side of the county draw commuters, and lake and rural parcels draw other buyers. A cash buyer does not depend on any of these markets, because the offer rests on the house, the title and the tax status.

faqs.q: When are Anderson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Under S.C. Code 12-45-70, property taxes are payable from September 30 to January 15. Penalties begin January 16 or 30 days after mailing, whichever is later.

faqs.q: What are the penalties for paying late?
faqs.a: The penalty is 3% after the due date, another 7% after February 1 and another 5% after March 16. After that the treasurer issues an execution.

faqs.q: How long do I have to dispute my assessment?
faqs.a: When the assessor mails an assessment notice, the owner has 90 days to send written notice of objection. Ask the Anderson County Assessor for the form.

faqs.q: What if the tax bill went to the old owner?
faqs.a: The penalty statute says the treasurer shall waive the penalty if the notice went to the prior owner and the new owner got no timely notice. Ask the treasurer in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Anderson County house that owes tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer and the title company can pay open tax from the sale proceeds at closing.
